about: The scenario-outcome matrix (docs/verification/SCENARIOS.md). Each scenario: an impactor, a target, the harness case that plays it (a wall-matrix case, structures/vehicle-lab/wall-matrix.mjs, or a test-bed trial, structures/vehicle-lab/trials.mjs) and what the real world does, as checks the judge (scripts/verify/scenarios.mjs) derives from scripts/verify/scenario-physics.mjs and the scene's geometry. `intent` marks where physics leaves a range and the matrix chooses within it.

cannonball.source: server/src/city.rs city_ball_mass_kg, city_ball_speed_ms; steel 7850 kg/m3 (r 0.687 m)

ball100.source: the impact study's 100 kg steel ball (r 0.146 m)

truck10.source: monster truck 5000 kg (reality.mjs: Monster Jam 4500-5500 kg); body 2.24 m wide, to 2.34 m above ground (prepared asset bounds)

truck20.source: the monster truck at street speed (72 km/h)

truck30.source: the monster truck at its top speed (reality.mjs 25-32 m/s)

coast24.source: the monster truck floored for 5 s on the flat lane (~24 m/s), then let go: nothing struck, the road only

debris700.source: the test bed's thrown wall panel (Vibe Town p90 chunk, 700 kg as a ball r 0.55 m) at 15 m/s

veneer.name: brick-veneer house, wall between studs
veneer.resistanceWhy: 4 C24 38x89 studs across a 2.24 m truck, 2.4 m pinned: P_u = 4 f_m W / L = 3.0 kN each (f_m,mean 36 MPa), end nails 0.5-1 kN (EN 1995-1-1 8.3); the 90 mm veneer in flexure f_xk1 0.1-0.4 MPa (EN 1996-1-1 Table 3.6) adds a few kN

masonry.name: free-standing masonry wall 7 x 2.5 x 0.25 m
masonry.resistanceWhy: cantilever from its base: f_xk1 0.1-0.4 MPa x 7 x 0.25^2/6 + its weight's restoring N t/2 (81 kN x 0.125 m) = 17-39 kN m, over a 1.2 m contact height

mailbox.name: post box on its post
mailbox.resistanceWhy: a pillar box's anchors or a post box's post (steel post ~50 x 3 CHS: W_pl f_u ~ 2-3 kN m at ~1 m; anchor bolts M10-M12 at 30-60 kN in tension, EN 1993-1-8 Table 3.4, at a lever of ~0.2 m)

streetlight.name: street light column
streetlight.resistanceWhy: 114.3 x 4 CHS S355 (EN 40-5): W_el f_y 13 kN m to W_pl f_u 20 kN m, at a 0.8-1.3 m contact

tree.name: street tree trunk
tree.resistanceWhy: sycamore, green MOR 45 MPa (Wood Handbook FPL-GTR-282 Table 5-3a): M_u = MOR pi d^3/32 = 35-283 kN m for d 0.2-0.4 m, at ~1 m

brick-house.name: one-storey brick house, 0.25 m wall
brick-house.resistanceWhy: punching around the truck's front: perimeter 2 x 2.34 + 2.24 = 6.9 m x 0.25 m of bed and head joints at f_vk0 0.1-0.3 MPa (EN 1996-1-1 Table 3.4)

scenarios.why: a stud is ~50 J to break in bending (C24): nothing to a 19 MJ ball; the top plate spans the gap (one stud of a wall)

the corner posts go: the top plates over the corner then cantilever ~0.6-1.4 m under ~2 kN of roof, against a double flat plate's ~1.5 kN m (C24): a local sag at the corner is within physics, so the roof is measured
from above at 45 degrees: through tiles, battens, a rafter or two and the ceiling; the rafters either side carry on

locality measured: an unreinforced masonry panel struck out of plane cracks along its mortar joints to its supports (yield lines; f_xk 0.1-0.4 MPa, EN 1996-1-1 Table 3.6), so breaks beyond the hole are physical

the owner's meteor-into-roof (2026-10-08): from above at 45 degrees it meets the roof first (tiles, battens, rafters, ceiling: ~70 kg of plug and a few kJ against 1.08 GJ), so it goes through at ~140 m/s; a 4 m rock then reaches the floor before it clears the roof plane, so the speed is judged one roof depth past first contact and the ground is reported separately

the owner's meteor-through-upper-wall (2026-10-08): at 4.4 m, its bottom 2.4 m up, near-level from the street, it meets the upper brick wall first and leaves the 11 m deep house through the far wall with its bottom still 1.9 m above grade: the whole path is the structure, nothing else

scenarios.intent: through: 0.30 m of stone against an NDRC perforation thickness of 0.36 m is inside the formula's scatter; the matrix chooses the hole

scenarios.why: locality measured: an unreinforced masonry panel struck out of plane cracks along its mortar joints to its supports (yield lines; f_xk 0.1-0.4 MPa, EN 1996-1-1 Table 3.6), so breaks beyond the hole are physical

locality measured: an unreinforced masonry panel struck out of plane cracks along its mortar joints to its supports (yield lines; f_xk 0.1-0.4 MPa, EN 1996-1-1 Table 3.6), so breaks beyond the hole are physical
387 kN (EN 1991-1-7) against 170-520 kN of punching resistance: a stop or a breach are both physical; measured

scenarios.intent: through: 775 kN against 170-520 kN; the owner's bar (2026-10-07) that a truck at 20 m/s gets through the first wall

scenarios.why: the lab trial: floored from 50 m (about 21 m/s at the house), through the front wall, the house and out of the back wall; through = the truck's middle past the back brick face (z 27.9)

the lab trial: floored from 50 m into the wall; the wall's base moment capacity (12-45 kN at the contact) is ~20x under the 0.8 MN the truck brings; through = its middle past the wall's back face (z 20.125)

19.2 MJ and 639 kN s into a 5 t truck: stopping the ball inside its own diameter needs ~6.7 MN on the truck's structure, which a frame of ~10 chromoly tubes (266 kN each) cannot give: it punches through, and what it passes through goes
1.08 GJ, a 4 m rock onto a 4.3 x 2.2 m truck: it sweeps most of it
a lesser hit: 180 kJ through the side at body height costs what it passes through; the truck drives on

the lab's coast trial: floored from bare ground onto the paved lane (a 25 mm asphalt lip, build-lab.mjs) at ~23 m/s, then let go. A road car takes a 25 mm lip at 80 km/h undamaged. Vehicle2's rigid tyre and massless wheel hand the lip to the damper in one tick (80 kN on each rear wheel, 6x static, 2026-10-08), which steel corners carry by yielding (EN 1993-1-1 3.2.2): nothing breaks

700 kg at 15 m/s on a tyre: F = v sqrt(k m_r) = 204 kN (k 300 kN/m, m_r 614 kg) against ten M22 10.9 lug studs' 1.95 MN in shear (ISO 898-1, 0.62 f_ub A_s) and a monster truck's 250-500 kN design landing load
a meteor clipping the cab roof by 30 cm: the roof it passes through goes; the wheels are nowhere near it
a steel post box on a post: its anchors give way at a few kN against 0.78 MN
114.3 x 4 CHS S355 column: W_pl f_u ~ 20 kN m, so ~17 kN at 1.2 m; folding it over takes ~M_p pi/2 = 31 kJ of the truck's 1 MJ (EN 12767 tests knock columns down)
a street tree's trunk (sycamore, green MOR 45 MPa, Wood Handbook Table 5-3a): M_u = MOR pi d^3/32, 119 kN m at d 0.3 m, against 0.78 MN x ~1 m

fleet.about: The fleet cars into the masonry wall and through the veneer house at street speed (the lab's floored trials, ~20 m/s at the target): EN 1991-1-7's 300 kN/m gives each 0.4-0.6 MN against the walls' 8-45 kN, so each gets through the first wall, keeps its wheels and drives on.
